Perfumers have always been the object of admiration in Bloomville, but Marlowe seemed to be the exception.
Whenever Marlowe promotes a new perfume, everyone keeps their distance, afraid that getting too close might cause them to become another "victim."
Yet there are still those who, swayed by his passionate pitches, end up passing out on the spot.
The elder was deeply troubled by this.
As there was nothing else to be done, the elder made Marlowe stand near his own home to promote his products. That way, whoever was unfortunate enough to fall prey to his concoctions could be dragged back to the elder’s house for timely treatment.
The elder had worn himself out worrying over Marlowe.
In fact, the elder’s favor toward Marlowe was not without reason.
Marlowe was born with a "bad nose," unable to tell one scent from another.
As a child, he tried learning perfume blending like everyone else, and eagerly brought his very first perfume to the elder.
The elder was overwhelmed by the stench, which smelled like "rotten honey cake"... and passed out on the spot.
When he woke up and saw Marlowe watching him with concern, he had no choice but to say he only passed out from delight—the scent was simply too wonderful.
Marlowe was so excited that he decided then that he was a genius perfumer.
And so, even though his perfume promotions continued to meet resistance, he never gave up his pursuit of perfume making.
————
Marlowe’s belief that he was a genius perfumer wasn’t just because of the elder’s compliment.
Though he couldn’t smell the sea breeze or the flowers, he could perceive certain... unusual scents.
For instance, he might catch whiffs of money, freedom, and warmth from people.
He even once caught an Aniimo thief.
Some said Aeolus had closed one door for Marlowe but opened a window.
Others argued it was just Marlowe’s imagination.
Yet when Marlowe crafted "Perfect Mistake," which was later regarded as a legendary perfume, a quiet shift began in people’s minds.
Could he really be a genius? The people of Bloomville started wondering.
